title: Minneapolis autonomous vehicles: City Council could override mayor's veto
key_facts: On 1 Oct the Minneapolis City Council voted 7-6 for an ordinance requiring a licensed human safety monitor inside driverless rideshare vehicles.
The ordinance would also require AV companies like Waymo to hold a city licence and pay the monitor at least minimum wage.
Waymo called it a 'de-facto ban' and Mayor Jacob Frey vetoed it.
The council votes on whether to override the veto on 15 Oct; nine votes are needed and it is unclear whether they have them.
Council member Robin Wonsley said that if the override fails she will bring a resolution centred on rideshare worker jobs.
On 14 Oct St. Paul's council approved a study of driverless vehicles instead of immediate regulation, with no timeline.
quote_evidence: The 7-6 vote put Minneapolis on track to become the first U.S. city to require a person in the driver’s seat for robotaxis.
Waymo called the move a "de-facto ban," and Mayor Jacob Frey swiftly vetoed the measure.
It is also not clear whether Minneapolis council members had the nine votes needed to override Frey’s veto.
why_it_matters_hint: A vote today decides whether Minneapolis becomes the first US city to require humans inside robotaxis.
event_date: Council vote 1 Oct; veto fight and override vote 15 Oct 2026
